# Global utilities

Six utilities cross every workspace. None of them creates a canonical object;
each reads canonical registers and projects.

## Action center

Route: `/actions`

Project every obligation the authorized capacity currently owes, drawn from the registers that already hold them.

- Reads: finding, decision, evidence, work-item, risk, claim
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: Creates no tasks of its own. If an obligation is not recorded on a canonical object, it does not appear here.

## Universal search

Route: `/search`

Find any authorized governed record across the shell without leaking the existence of others.

- Reads: decision, finding, evidence, claim, enterprise-capability, work-item
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: Authorization filters the candidate set before matching or counting. Counts, facets, and suggestions come from authorized records only.

## Notifications

Route: `/notifications`

Surface the small set of states where a human owes a response or must know that work has stopped.

- Reads: finding, decision, evidence, risk, claim
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: A state change with no owed response is recorded, not notified.

## My workspaces

Route: `/workspaces`

Show which workspaces the current capacity may enter, and which are held behind a gate.

- Reads: workspace-definition, acting-capacity
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: Membership places a capacity in a workspace. It authorizes no record inside it.

## Knowledge and help

Route: `/help`

Explain the system while keeping governing policy visibly separate from explanatory help.

- Reads: policy-rule, standard, knowledge-object
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: Help text never governs. Only policies, standards, procedures, and boundary statements do.

## Profile and acting capacity

Route: `/profile`

Make it unambiguous who is acting, in what capacity, and what that capacity may not do.

- Reads: acting-capacity, person-reference
- Creates canonical objects: none
- Boundary: Holds a synthetic operator handle only. No name, no contact details, no personal data of any kind.
